name: NJM8901 / NJM8901E
tagline: Entry-tier JRC JFET dual (13 nV/√Hz, 20 V/µs) using MUSES know-how; reportedly easy-listening with light bass.

lineage.note: Entry tier with bipolar NJM8801 and NJM4582, below MUSES8820/8920/8832 and MUSES01/02/03 (stereo.jp).
Successor to New Japan Radio (merger reportedly January 2022); distributors now credit Nisshinbo.

part_numbers.note: Base part number; no manufacturer lifecycle page seen.
EMP8 (SOP8 JEDEC 150 mil) SMD. Sold by Mouser, chip1stop, Akizuki, Kyohritsu eleshop.
Tape-and-reel NJM8901E. Profusion alone marks it obsolete; Nisshinbo has not confirmed.

key_specs.value: 5 MHz typ (open-loop gain 86 dB min / 110 dB typ)
JFET (BiFET); CMRR 70 dB min / 90 dB typ

reputation.summary: A niche Japanese-market part, not a legend. Akizuki sells it as a 'HiFi op-amp'; one auction seller calls it 'mass-production MUSES'. The only listening report, a 2023 guiblo blog comparison, finds it easy to listen to with light bass, while MUSES8820D gives deeper, weightier bass. A Japanese YouTube comparison reportedly includes it. No measurements found.
sonic_descriptors: light bass (低音があっさり目)
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in DACs and headphone amps (needs adapter)
I/V converters, thanks to low JFET bias current
Budget step up from NJM4580/NJM4558-class duals (inferred)
caveats: Thin evidence: one unblinded blog comparison and an unchecked YouTube shoot-out; descriptors come from a single listener.
NJM8901E is SMD (EMP8 = SOP8 150 mil); DIP8 sockets need an adapter.
Offset 2 mV typ, 10 mV max: use coupling capacitors or a DC servo in DC-coupled stages.
Needs at least ±4 V supply; unsuited to low-voltage rails.
Lifecycle uncertain: Profusion flags NJM8901E-TE2 obsolete.

counterfeit_notes: No NJM8901-specific counterfeit reports found, though none were sought directly. Low-volume part seen at brokers (veswin, censtry, ovaga); the reel code is flagged obsolete. Buy from Mouser, chip1stop, Akizuki or Kyohritsu eleshop.

open_questions: Did Ver. 2014-10-28 change any spec from Ver. 2012-02-07? Which version is the Mouser 'E3' copy?
Is NJM8901 on Nisshinbo's maintenance or EOL lists? FindChips shows no stock; no notice found.
Does a DIP8 NJM8901D exist? Is supply current per device or per channel?
Did the JRC-to-Nisshinbo transition bring a fab move? Is NL8902 its intended replacement?
What does the YouTube comparison (zS7Z64YsgOg) show? Any bench measurements?

claims_confirmed: High-quality audio J-FET dual balancing MUSES technology with mass production (https://en.sekorm.com/doc/2511119.html).
13 nV/√Hz, 20 V/µs, 5 MHz, THD 0.003% (Av=10), ±4.0–±18 V, Icc 4–6 mA, Vio 2–10 mV, Ib 30–400 pA, Avd 86–110 dB, CMR 70–90 dB (https://en.sekorm.com/doc/2511119.html).
Vendor copy: original process tuning and assembly technology; JFET low bias suits I/V converters (https://akizukidenshi.com/catalog/g/g108175/ ; https://eleshop.jp/shop/g/gE91121/).
Entry tier with NJM8801 and NJM4582 in JRC's audio line (https://stereo.jp/?p=3614).
Akizuki sells NJM8901E as '2回路入HiFiオペアンプ' (https://akizukidenshi.com/catalog/g/g108175/).
Mouser hosts an NJM8901 datasheet in its NJR folder (https://www.mouser.com/ds/2/294/NJM8901_DataSheetE3-262000.pdf).

Listed at Mouser under NJR and chip1stop under Nisshinbo (https://www.mouser.com/ProductDetail/NJR/NJM8901E?qs=sajaCoHCXPTKvhQTAp2OpA%3D%3D ; https://www.chip1stop.com/USA/en/product/detail?partId=NJR1-0013450).
Nisshinbo Micro Devices (formerly New Japan Radio) is the current maker (https://www.censtry.com/product/nisshinbo-micro-devices-inc/njm8901e.html).
Nisshinbo released the NL8902 JFET dual, news dated 2025-05-13 (https://www.nisshinbo-microdevices.co.jp/en/about/info/20250513.html).
Several ex-JRC op-amps are maintenance / planned-discontinuation parts; NJM8901's inclusion unconfirmed (https://foxtango101.blog.jp/archives/19678237.html).
An NJM8901 datasheet copy is marked Ver.2012-02-07, 'High Quality Audio J-FET Input Dual Operational Amplifier': https://xonelec.com/mpn/nisshinbo/njm8901e
FindChips returns no NJM8901 stock and suggests NJM8801E: https://www.findchips.com/search/NJM8901
